about: Card 70's four navigation symbols, each meaning one thing on every screen: hollow triangle with a bar = switch item, solid triangle = step a move, blue circled triangle = play a line (the only blue), curled arrow = reset. Graded by gate 227 (TC-R376..380) on a trial bundle at 375x761 with his insets and at 320x568, over three of its states (Play mid-game, a training puzzle after one move, the lesson demo at ply 4); the whole gate walks sixteen states and the desktop Play moves panel and Review row, and is the suite's. NOT COVERED: worded start buttons with a decorative triangle (named in the gate header, a copy question), the Review best-move chip row (card 76, on the Desk), Apple emoji ink and his phone.

breaks.name: item-drawn-solid
breaks.why: the previous/next-item triangle is filled in, so going to another puzzle looks like stepping a move

breaks.name: step-back-to-the-chevron
breaks.why: the move step goes back to batch 13's white chevron instead of the solid triangle

breaks.name: lesson-play-is-a-plain-triangle
breaks.why: the lesson's Play draws the plain solid move triangle, not the blue circled one, so playing the line looks like stepping one move
